structured_output.reasoning: The incident's frustrated message ("That's not what I asked; the request was a one-file note") and the following exchange referencing an unrequested "fake demo" the agent added are a textbook instance of the failure pattern the remedy targets: user requests a narrow, single-artifact change (one file, one note) and the agent instead delivers extra unrequested scope (a demo). The remedy text explicitly calls out this exact scenario — "implement exactly that scope... Do not perform a broader rewrite, refactor, or add extra unrequested artifacts (demos, new files, restructuring)" — and requires the agent to ask before adding wider changes. Had this rule been active, it would have directed the agent to stick to the one-file note and flag/ask about the demo idea rather than building it, directly addressing the root cause of the user's frustration. There's no material gap visible in this specific incident's evidence — the remedy's own example enumeration (demos) matches the artifact that caused the complaint.
